claims.text: The consistency of pretrained language models with respect to factual knowledge is poor under meaning-preserving input alternations.
Consistency in pretrained language models exhibits high variance between different relations.
Representational spaces of pretrained language models have poor structure for representing knowledge robustly.
A method is proposed for improving model consistency in pretrained language models.

evidence.description: Evaluation on the ParaRel resource demonstrates poor consistency across all tested pretrained language models.
Evaluation across 38 relations shows high variance in consistency scores depending on the relation.
Analysis of the representational spaces of pretrained language models suggests structural deficiencies for robust knowledge representation.

methodologies.name: ParaRel evaluation framework
methodologies.description: A benchmark dataset and evaluation process using 328 cloze-style English paraphrase queries across 38 relations to measure PLM consistency.

limitations.text: Pretrained language models have poor representational structure and are currently not suitable for representing knowledge robustly.
